Throughput measured at real N=15,400 / |E|=310,867, batch 64, 30 steps, rank 8, fwd+bwd on MPS. sparse.mm 952 ms/rollout = 2.07 h per 5e5 steps (FASTEST, now the default); dense 2425 ms = 5.26 h; gather 12279 ms = 26.65 h. A1 gate 2 PASSED at full scale on MPS: all three couplings bit-identical (agreement 1.000000, maxdiff 0.00e+00, 48,727 spikes). No thermal throttling over 120 s sustained (1.01x). Resident memory 2,056 MB; an earlier 128 MB figure was a broken metric and was fixed. 246,400 trainable adapter params at r=8. P5 verdict: 2.07 h/run means ~83 h for the 40-run series on the laptop - confirmatory belongs on the CUDA host as A1 already required; P5's budget there stays UNVERIFIED pending fly-ky7.4.

MiniCard v1 engine implemented per P2, 21 tests, 52 total green. 10-card pool, mana min(turn,10), board cap 5, summoning sickness, fatigue, hand cap 7 with burn, 3-level legality-masked actions, terminal +1/-1/0, seed-deterministic, illegal actions raise. Two scripted opponents (greedy-face, board-control). SANITY SIMULATION FOUND A DESIGN DEFECT the unit tests could not: at P2's HP=20 racing beat trading 88% and games ended turn 5-7, so the optimum was degenerate and no working memory was needed - which would have left no room for a topology effect and not exercised the CX rationale. Amendment A2 raises START_HP to 30; verified control now dominates, games 10-22 turns / 72-139 decisions. My first diagnosis (blaming the removal of taunt) was wrong and measurement refuted it. Residual: control mirror favours player two 60.8%, so seats must alternate and per-seat rates be reported.

P4 controls implemented and validated at real scale. 22 tests, 74 total green. Key identity: directed double-edge swap permutes only 'post' ('pre' never moves), so out-degree, in-degree, each weight's own source, and Dale's law hold by construction. 31M swaps in 11.6 s vectorised, 2.2% of edges survive. Matching at N=15,400: every tolerance-0 quantity identical across arms (N, |E|, density, degree means, rho=0.95, E/I/mod 10,795/3,312/1,293). Graded ladder achieved: shuffled preserves degree tail bit-for-bit (2,843/2,763) and the giant SCC (14,846 vs 14,841) while reciprocity falls 0.225->0.021 and clustering 0.267->0.075; random destroys the tail (42/65) and halves the SCC (7,703). Dynamical calibration reaches 5.449/5.465/4.975 Hz. CORRECTION recorded as R5: P4's second step was justified as preventing inter-arm saturation differences, but all arms fire 0.000 Hz at unit input after spectral normalisation, so without it NO arm learns; inter-arm matching is actually delivered by the structural step (gains differ 3%).

Encoder, codec and SpikingPolicy implemented. 20 tests, 94 total green. FIRST END-TO-END RUN SUCCEEDED: a 15,400-neuron FlyWire substrate (rho=0.95, calibrated gain 3.587, 1,042 sensory inputs, 44 descending outputs, 542,591 trainable params) played a complete MiniCard game - 34 actions, 8 turns, result -1, ZERO illegal actions, 13 ms per decision. The loss is expected from an untrained policy; the zero is the result that matters, because legality is structural rather than learned. IO wiring follows super-class (afferent in, descending out), computed once on the real graph and reused as indices by every arm per P3. Defect found and fixed: act() built its observation tensor on CPU regardless of module device, crashing the first MPS run; unit tests missed it because they never moved the policy off CPU, and a regression test now covers it. Two silent-substrate traps hit: head WEIGHT gradients vanish while BIAS gradients survive when the substrate does not spike, and the 40-neuron toy fixture needed recurrent weights of 25 before signal reached the readout (4 and 10 left it silent) - third independent confirmation that P4's 5 Hz calibration is load-bearing.

PPO with GAE implemented and the pipeline demonstrably LEARNS. 17 tests, 109 total green. On a 500-neuron substrate with mirror decks and alternating opponents, 24k agent decisions took overall return -1.000 -> -0.244 and vs board_control -1.000 -> +0.391; the scripted board_control bot scores exactly 0.000 against itself, so the trained policy now beats the bot it trained against (~70%). Episodes per rollout fell 153 -> 45, i.e. the agent survives 3.4x longer. Critical correctness test passes: replayed log-prob reproduces the stored one so PPO's ratio starts at exactly 1. MAJOR CONFOUND FOUND AND REMOVED: MiniCard defaulted to asymmetric decks ('aggro','control') pinned to seats, so alternating seats also alternated decks - and after A2 raised HP to 30, NO policy wins with the aggro deck (board_control: 0.0% over 200 games from either seat). Half of every rollout was unwinnable and half the gradient was noise. A2 fixed one degeneracy and silently created another. P2 never required different decks, so the primary config is now a mirror matchup with no amendment needed. Open item recorded: an untrained spiking policy scores -1.000 where uniform-random scores -0.580, so initialisation is degenerate, not random.

P5 analysis implemented: IQM, stratified bootstrap over seeds AND episodes, probability of improvement with ties as half, Holm step-down, and compare_arms delivering the exact pre-registered decision. 18 tests, 127 total green. CHARACTERISED BEFORE ANY RUN (R8): false positive rate 0.010 at nominal alpha 0.05 - conservative, because P5 requires both Holm-p < alpha AND a 95% CI excluding zero while a one-sided 0.05 test matches a 90% interval, putting the effective level near 0.025. Power at 10 seeds: +5pp 0.195, +10pp 0.715, +15pp 0.975, +20pp 1.000; power vs seeds at +10pp: 5->0.465, 10->0.715, 20->0.935. Decision: keep 10 seeds, publish the power curve, and report any null as 'no effect of at least ~10 pp detected' rather than 'no effect'. Also recorded D2: training against real Hearthstone is unavailable - fireplace/hearthbreaker/sabberstone/hearthstone-sim are all uninstallable, python-hearthstone is metadata only, hslog is a log parser, and automating the retail client is refused on terms-of-service grounds.

Harness implemented; 146 tests green. The pilot it enabled found a BLOCKING design flaw and two amendments followed. A3: P4's rho=0.95 understated the weight scale by ~1780x for a spiking substrate - 100% of 15,710 spikes stayed in directly-driven input neurons, nothing propagated, and all three arms returned byte-identical scores; replaced by branching-ratio calibration measured with no external drive, each arm scaled individually. A4: spike-count readout leaves the median output unit at ZERO variance across game states unless exactly at criticality; replaced by mean pre-reset membrane potential, and P4's 5 Hz input calibration removed as ill-posed once branching is fixed. Two hypotheses were measured and refuted along the way (hop distance - outputs are 1-3 hops away, 25 of 44 adjacent; gain - a 1000x increase changed nothing); the real cause is sparsity, ~534 of 15,400 neurons spiking. Verified after both: every readout unit varies with game state and arms give different representations. NOT yet a topology result - no learning has run. The pilot must be re-run under the amended protocol.

tests/test_run_pilot_wiring.py (7 tests) covers build_real_graph with monkeypatched loaders: the manifest is verified before any table is read, a ManifestMismatch stops the run with nothing loaded, labels reach select_io_indices as a positional array in neuron order rather than as a root_id-indexed Series, edges are remapped to positions in sorted-id order, Dale signs are requested in that same order, and pick_device honours an explicit request.

Measured and written up in three artifacts. window_cost_v783.json locates the cliff: sparse is linear to 200 steps (1279 ms, 4291 MB) then fails to finish 250 or 300 in 240 s, and batching is nearly free (56x the work for 14 percent more time at 30 steps). gather_at_window_v783.json answers the budget question differently than expected: gather clears the full 300-step window at 274 ms and 961 MB, batch 8 is the ceiling on 12 GB, batch 16 spills to host memory under WDDM (14926 MB peak on a 12282 MiB card, 12x slower) and batch 32 raises OutOfMemoryError. mode_equivalence_v783.json confirms the modes are byte-identical on the real subset, so the swap is a configuration choice. run_pilot now takes --coupling.

dale_signs now separates the two failures that both collapsed into a silent 0: a neuron absent from the transmitter table, and a transmitter category outside Dale's six. It counts them, names the unknown categories in the message, and raises ManifestMismatch above a tolerance. The library default is permissive (max_unsigned_fraction=1.0) so the documented mapping and its existing five-neuron test are untouched; run_pilot passes MAX_UNSIGNED_FRACTION=0.01 explicitly, because the strictness belongs on the path whose output is evidence. Six tests in tests/test_run_pilot_wiring.py.
